meta.source_data_tree_note: git tree id of data/ when generated; equals `git rev-parse <commit>:data` for any commit with the same data
meta.encoding: Zone lists follow hit_locations order. zone_multiplier {row: R}: B[z] = bone_rows.Universal[z] × bone_rows[R][z] (R null: Universal alone); zone_multiplier null: B[z] = 1. A factor {k} gives factor[z] = k × B[z]; {zones} lists the 12 factors. Damage = S × factor[z] (× the falloff curve at the distance, keys in metres). Armor {k} multiplies the unarmored factor on the hit locations the item covers; {zones} gives those factors. entries are the entries with a factor other than 1 on every hit location, zone_entries the extra ones per hit location. A file reference is [index into meta.files, field] or an index. A source's doc is a key of meta.docs and a direct case's case a key of meta.cases. A direct hit's source context is source_context, weapon_tag, caliber, Meta.Damage.DamageType.Projectile and, when has_arming_delay, Kinetic.Impact.ExplosiveBlunt (§7.6); a blast hit's is source_context and the ring's radius tag. Blast armor factors apply only if the armor tag reaches a blast hit (armor-hook-paths). Numbers are rounded to 6 significant digits.

cases.direct_not_exploding: Direct hit that is not exploding: S = BaseDamage (when a hit explodes is not traced)
cases.before_arming: Before arming (flight time below ArmingDelay): S = ExplosiveBluntDamage

items.text: The hit-location asset is picked by the target actor's class (ClassToHitLocations).
The hit location is an exact FName match of the raw FHitResult.BoneName in DamageHitLocations: no parent walk, and an unmapped bone gives an empty tag (no hit location).
DamageImpactRemap is never applied for damage: its reader has 3 callers, all animation or ragdoll. spine_05 is Torso.Upper for damage.

The hit bodies are PA_TPCharacter_Simplified's; all 20 map to a hit location. spine_01 and spine_02 have no body, so a live player never produces them. Mutable adds each helmet's single head body, which maps to Head.

Radial damage: the gathered hits pass the character's IWDDamageable filter (dropped in one seat state, otherwise one hit per component). Each kept hit is its own evaluation, tagged Radius.Inner or .Outer, with that hit's bone as the hit location.
Kinetic.Impact.ExplosiveBlunt is added only on a projectile's direct-impact path, so entries 7, 117, 142 and 143 never apply to blast damage; entries 102–116 do.
Against a character, the explosive-actor path is the thrown object's contact damage (source Kinetic.Impact.Throwable, DamageType.Impact), applied once per contact on the contacted bone.

On foot, 0x6F042A0 traces the back-blast cone. In a seat, 0x6F06EB0 hits the occupants of the shooter's vehicle with synthetic hits, the shooter included. Only Launcher_04, RPG7 and CGM4 enable back-blast.

assumptions: rules from DamagePipeline §4-§7 only, through _tools/damage_tables.py: every selected entry multiplies the running amount, the total is clamped at 0 (§6)

§7.7 event: hostile alignment, FMJ (no ammo-modifier tag), a direct hit with no ricochet or penetration, no instigator tags, target outside any vehicle; point blank unless the falloff curve is applied
armor: only the piece whose CoveredHitLocations holds the hit location reaches the rules (Auth_GetArmorDamageEvent, §7.6); every durability stage has the same R in the data (§7.5)
an absent cooked property is its class default (bHasArmingDelay false)
bone factor U × W: U from row Universal, W from the first source-context tag naming a row or its direct parent, 1.0 with none (§7.1); Meta.Damage.Explosive.Drone is exempt

blast hits: one evaluation per hit with that hit's bone as the hit location and no ExplosiveBlunt (verifier round 6 (doc text pending)); source context = the projectile's source tag, DamageEntityData.Context and the radius tag (radial-context), so W = 1; the blast amount itself is not traced (radial-amount)

not_traced.text: Blast damage: which DamageValues field is the starting amount, the falloff arithmetic, and which radius separates Meta.Damage.Explosive.Radius.Inner from .Outer. GameMechanics §14 says BaseDamage and ExplosiveRadius feed the Calibre rules and falloff is ExplosiveDamageFallOff, without a formula.
not_traced.data: Projectile assets carry BaseDamage, ExplosiveRadius, EffectiveExplosiveRadius, ExplosiveDamageFallOff and on some MinimumExplosiveDamage (values per source).

not_traced.text: Which of the character's components the radial gather hits. Known (verifier round 6 (doc text pending)): one hit per component after the IWDDamageable filter 0x6E6DCC0, each hit its own evaluation with its bone's hit location.
not_traced.data: No data field describes the gather.

not_traced.text: Which tags a blast hit's source context carries besides the source tag and the radius tag (weapon tag, caliber id). The blast factors here use the projectile's source tag, its DamageEntityData.Context and the radius tag, so the bone factor's W is 1 on blast hits.
not_traced.data: Entries 108–116 need only the source tag and a radius tag.

not_traced.text: When a projectile hit is bExploding. §7.6: an exploding hit skips both scales, the armor hook and ModifyDamage on the projectile path; what sets bExploding is not stated, so whether an armed launcher, shell or cannon round ever deals the direct-hit amount is open.
not_traced.data: Projectile assets carry bHasArmingDelay and ArmingDelay (seconds of flight time, §7.6).

not_traced.text: Detonation damage of grenades, C4, mines, claymores, IEDs and the Molotov. Against a character 0x6CA8730 is only the thrown object's contact damage (verifier round 6 (doc text pending)); the detonation's path, amount and tags are not traced.

not_traced.text: Whether the target hook Auth_GetArmorDamageEvent (§7.6) runs on paths other than the projectile's direct impact (blast, back-blast, melee, actor impact, thrown contact). It decides whether an armor tag reaches entries 102–106 and 138–144.
Whether DT_GlobalDamage_ArmorData's rows are evaluated for a character hit. §5's walk for a character starts at Meta.Damage.Infantry and gives one group; the armor rows are keyed by armor tags.

categories.label: Bullets
categories.note: One event per hit from the projectile data and the firing weapon (§7.6): S = BaseDamage × speed scale × distance curve. Entry 5 multiplies by Universal × weapon row for the hit location (§7.1); a covering helmet or armor piece adds entries 138/140 (§7.3).

categories.label: Explosives and launchers
categories.note: A direct impact goes through the projectile path: before arming S is ExplosiveBluntDamage and the source carries Kinetic.Impact.ExplosiveBlunt, so entry 7 applies the bone factor and entries 142–143 armor durability; cannon rounds take entry 10. An exploding hit skips ModifyDamage there (§7.6). The blast goes through the radial path: one evaluation per hit component, tagged Radius.Inner or .Outer, with the hit bone's location and without ExplosiveBlunt, so entries 7, 117, 142 and 143 never apply to it and 102–116 do (verifier round 6 (doc text pending)). The blast amount and falloff are not traced. Grenades, C4 and mines detonate through a path that is not traced.

categories.label: Other
categories.note: Melee, actor impact and thrown-object contact match no bone entry (5, 7, 10 need Bullet, ExplosiveBlunt or Cannon, §3.1), so the factor is the same on every hit location. Entry 144 reduces melee damage on an armored target by R (§7.5).

model.centres_note: world-space bounding-box centre of each body's mesh, metres, glTF axes (+Y up, facing +Z, origin at the feet), from accessor min/max through the composed node transforms
notes: Hit-trace bodies: PA_TPCharacter_Simplified is the PhysicsAsset of SK_DefaultCharacter (B_WDMoverPlayerCharacter CharacterMesh.SkeletalMesh) and of SK_TP_Male_000, the reference mesh of MUT_TP_Character that builds the runtime mesh. CharacterMesh.BodyInstance.CollisionEnabled is QueryOnly (profile Custom).
Ragdoll uses a different asset: DA_WDRagdollMovement.PhysicsAsset is PA_TPCharacter_Simplified_Physics. It is not shown here.
Reference pose of SK_DefaultCharacter; in game the bodies follow the animated bones.
Origin at the feet (mesh component origin); the actor origin is 0.96 m higher. Facing +Z.

Helmets: MUT_TP_Character also lists five helmet physics assets (PA_Helmet_*), each with one body on head. Mutable adds that body to the character (verifier round 6), still the Head hit location; the merge rule is not traced, and the helmet bodies are not shown.
Whether Chaos builds query shapes from the six tapered-capsule bodies is unverified.

bone_rule.data: DamageHitLocations maps 22 bone names to tags
bone_rule.runtime: exact FName match of FHitResult.BoneName in the asset picked by the actor's class; no parent walk; an unmapped bone gives no hit location (0x6F01BB0, 0x6BB8D00; verifier round 6 (doc text pending))
bone_rule.unmapped: with no hit location, entries with a hit-location filter are not selected (§4 rule 4) and all armor tags are removed (§7.6)
bone_rule.impact_remap: DamageImpactRemap (spine_01 → pelvis, spine_05 → spine_04) is used by animation and ragdoll only, never for damage (0x6BB8D40; verifier round 6 (doc text pending))
bone_rule.live_player: spine_01 and spine_02 have no body in PA_TPCharacter_Simplified, so a live player never produces them; a helmet adds its own head body, which maps to Head (verifier round 6 (doc text pending))

sources.label: Thrown object contact
sources.why: 0x6CA8730 against a character is the thrown object's contact damage, applied once per contact on the contacted bone (verifier round 6 (doc text pending)). No infantry entry requires these tags, so the hit location changes no factor. The amount is not traced.

sources.label: Actor or vehicle impact
sources.why: 0x6E72D90 (§1.1) builds the event from the hitting actor's entity data plus DamageType.Impact; no infantry entry requires Impact, so nothing depends on the hit location. The amount is not traced.
